results.title: Verifier strategy
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A Verifier strategy for the model-checking game on a Kripke model $M$ is a map $\sigma$ from game positions to game positions such that, at every Verifier-owned position $p$ from which some move exists, there is a move from $p$ to $\sigma(p)$.

results.title: Finite plays consistent with a strategy
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Fix a Kripke model $M$ and a Verifier strategy $\sigma$. The finite plays from a position $p$ that follow $\sigma$ are the lists of positions defined inductively: the one-element list $[p]$ is such a play; and if the game has a move from $p$ to $q$, where $q$ is the position chosen by $\sigma$ at $p$ whenever Verifier owns $p$, then $p$ followed by any such play from $q$ is such a play from $p$.

results.title: Last position of a play
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The last position of a finite list of game positions is its final entry when the list is nonempty; the empty list has no last position.

results.title: Verifier has a winning strategy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a Kripke model $M$, an environment $\mathit{env}$ and a game position $p$, Verifier wins from $p$ when some Verifier strategy $\sigma$ in the model-checking game on $M$ wins from $p$ in environment $\mathit{env}$: every complete finite $\sigma$-consistent play from $p$ ends at a terminal winning position, and every infinite $\sigma$-consistent play from $p$ satisfies the parity condition.

results.title: Closed formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A μ-calculus formula $\varphi$ is closed when it is closed at depth $0$, that is, when it has no free variables.

results.title: Closedness is monotone in the depth
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a μ-calculus formula and let $d \le d'$ be natural numbers. If $\varphi$ is closed at depth $d$ (every free variable of $\varphi$ is less than $d$), then $\varphi$ is closed at depth $d'$: more enclosing binders can only bind more variables.

results.title: Closed formulas are environment-independent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a closed μ-calculus formula, that is, one with no free variables. For any two environments $\mathrm{env}$ and $\mathrm{env}'$, each assigning a set of worlds to every variable index, and every world $w$, $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$ under $\mathrm{env}$ if and only if it is satisfied at $w$ in $M$ under $\mathrm{env}'$.

results.title: The one-world reflexive Kripke model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Kripke model with a single world, which is related to itself, and a single atom, which is false at that world.

results.title: A least fixpoint over a vacuous greatest fixpoint
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The μ-calculus formula $\mu X.\, \nu Y.\, X$ over a one-element type of atoms: a least fixpoint whose body is a greatest fixpoint whose body is the variable $X$ bound by the outer least fixpoint, so the variable $Y$ bound by the inner greatest fixpoint never occurs.

results.title: The regression play stays on the cycle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the position at step $n$ of the regression play is the first, the second or the third cycle position.

results.title: The regression play has period three
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Number the positions of the regression play from $0$. For every natural number $n$, its position number $n + 3$ equals its position number $n$.

results.title: The regression play returns to its start every three steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Number the positions of the regression play of $\mu X.\,\nu Y.\,X$ from $0$. For every natural number $k$, its position number $3k$ is its starting position: the formula $\mu X.\,\nu Y.\,X$ at the unique world, with the empty binder stack.

results.title: The regression play is a play
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, in the model-checking game on the one-world regression model there is a move from the position at step $n$ of the regression play to the position at step $n + 1$.

results.title: Fixpoint-free formulas
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The fixpoint-free formulas over a type of atoms are built from atoms $p$, negated atoms $\neg p$, $\bot$ and $\top$ by conjunction $\varphi \land \psi$, disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$, necessity $\Box\varphi$ and possibility $\Diamond\varphi$.

results.title: Embedding of the fixpoint-free fragment into the μ-calculus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The map from fixpoint-free formulas to μ-calculus formulas defined by recursion: atoms, negated atoms, $\bot$ and $\top$ go to the same atom, negated atom, $\bot$ and $\top$, and $\varphi \wedge \psi$, $\varphi \vee \psi$, $\Box \varphi$ and $\Diamond \varphi$ go to the conjunction, disjunction, box and diamond of the images of $\varphi$ and $\psi$.

results.title: Backward-induction winning equals satisfaction on the fixpoint-free fragment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, environment $\mathit{env}$, fixpoint-free formula $\varphi$ and world $w$, $w$ lies in the backward-induction winning region of $\varphi$ if and only if $w$ satisfies the μ-calculus embedding of $\varphi$ in $M$ under $\mathit{env}$.

results.title: Size of a μ-calculus formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The size $|\varphi|$ of a μ-calculus formula $\varphi$ is the number of nodes of its syntax tree: an atom, a negated atom, a variable, $\bot$ and $\top$ have size $1$; $|\varphi \wedge \psi| = |\varphi \vee \psi| = |\varphi| + |\psi| + 1$; and $|\Box\varphi| = |\Diamond\varphi| = |\mu\varphi| = |\nu\varphi| = |\varphi| + 1$.

results.title: The partial inverse recovers fixpoint-free formulas
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every fixpoint-free formula $\varphi$, the partial inverse of the embedding of fixpoint-free formulas into μ-calculus formulas is defined at the image of $\varphi$ under the embedding, with value $\varphi$.

results.title: The embedding inverts the partial inverse
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every μ-calculus formula $\psi$ and every fixpoint-free formula $\varphi$: if the partial inverse of the embedding of fixpoint-free formulas into μ-calculus formulas is defined at $\psi$ with value $\varphi$, then the embedding sends $\varphi$ to $\psi$.

results.title: The fixpoint-free embedding is injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The embedding of fixpoint-free formulas into μ-calculus formulas is injective: distinct fixpoint-free formulas have distinct images.

results.title: The Wins-guided move is legal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a Kripke model $M$ and a game position $p$ owned by Verifier from which some move exists, the Wins-guided move at $p$ is a legal move of the model-checking game on $M$ from $p$.

results.title: Wins-guided strategy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a Kripke model $M$, the Wins-guided strategy is the Verifier strategy of the model-checking game on $M$ that chooses, at each game position $(\psi, w, s)$, the Wins-guided move at $(\psi, w, s)$. At every Verifier-owned position that has a move, this choice is a legal move.

results.title: Finite plays are nonempty
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\sigma$ a Verifier strategy and $p$ a game position. Every finite play from $p$ consistent with $\sigma$ is a nonempty list of positions.

results.title: Prepending to a nonempty play keeps the last position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a game position $p$ and a nonempty list $ps$ of game positions, the list obtained by prepending $p$ to $ps$ has the same last position as $ps$.

results.title: No infinite play from a fragment position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\varphi$ a fixpoint-free formula and $w$ a world. There is no sequence of game positions $p_0, p_1, p_2, \dots$ with $p_0 = (\varphi, w, [\,])$ (the embedded formula with the empty stack) such that each step from $p_n$ to $p_{n+1}$ is a move of the model-checking game in $M$. The reason is that every move strictly decreases the formula size.

results.title: Winning strategies stay winning along consistent moves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\mathit{env}$ an environment and $\sigma$ a Verifier strategy for the model-checking game on $M$. If $\sigma$ wins from a position $p$ in $\mathit{env}$, and $q$ is a position reachable from $p$ by one move that is the position chosen by $\sigma$ at $p$ whenever Verifier owns $p$, then $\sigma$ also wins from $q$ in $\mathit{env}$.

results.title: Hitting time of a continuous-time Markov chain

results.title: First-jump decomposition of a hitting time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: From a state `i ∉ A`, the hitting time of `A` is the first holding time plus the hitting time of the chain restarted after the first jump.

results.title: Hitting time from inside the target set is zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: From a state `i ∈ A`, the hitting time of `A` is `0` as soon as the first holding time is positive (which fails only on a null event, see `ctmcHoldingTime`).

results.title: Mean hitting time from inside the target set is zero

results.title: Minimality of the mean hitting time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Minimality of the mean hitting time (compare Norris 1997, §3.3): if every state off `A` has a positive exit rate, every `m : ι → ℝ≥0∞` with `1 / q i + ∑ⱼ Π i j m j ≤ m i` off `A` dominates `E_i H_A`.

results.title: Product moment of two hitting times, first-step equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: From `i ∉ A ∪ B` with `q i ≠ 0`, `E_i (H_A H_B) = (E_i H_A + E_i H_B) / q i + ∑ⱼ Π i j E_j (H_A H_B)` in `ℝ≥0∞`.

results.title: Product moment of hitting times from inside their union is zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: From a state of `A ∪ B`, the product moment of the hitting times of `A` and `B` is `0`.

results.title: Minimality of the product moment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `mA`, `mB` are supersolutions of the mean equations of `A` and `B` (as in `lintegral_ctmcHittingTime_le`) and `F` satisfies `(mA i + mB i) / q i + ∑ⱼ Π i j F j ≤ F i` off `A ∪ B`, then `F` dominates `E_i (H_A H_B)`.

results.title: Backward equations for the mean hitting time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Backward equations for the mean hitting time (compare Norris 1997, §3.3): if `m : ι → ℝ` is nonnegative and `(Q m) i = -1` for `i ∉ A`, then `E_i H_A ≤ m i` (so it is finite), `E_i H_A = 0` on `A`, and the real vector `E_i H_A` solves the same backward equations. With uniqueness of the solution, this identifies `E_i H_A`.

results.title: Backward equations for the product moment of two hitting times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `mA`, `mB`, `f` be nonnegative with `(Q mA) i = -1` off `A`, `(Q mB) i = -1` off `B` and `(Q f) i = -(mA i + mB i)` off `A ∪ B`. Then `E_i (H_A H_B) ≤ f i` (so it is finite), it is `0` on `A ∪ B`, and its real part `p` solves `(Q p) i = -(E_i H_A + E_i H_B)` off `A ∪ B`.

results.title: Edmonds' matroid partition theorem, arbitrary ground set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set, let $M$ be a matroid with ground set $E(M) \subseteq E$, let $S \subseteq E$ and let $k$ be a natural number. Then $S = J_1 \cup \dots \cup J_k$ for some sets $J_1, \dots, J_k$ that are independent in $M$ (not necessarily disjoint) if and only if $|X| \le k \, r_M(X)$ for every $X \subseteq S$, where $r_M(X)$ denotes the rank in $M$ of $X \cap E(M)$.

results.title: Edmonds' matroid partition theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set, let $M$ be a matroid whose ground set is all of $E$, let $S \subseteq E$ and let $k$ be a natural number. results.title: Independent codes for the modular cycle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $q$ and $n$ be natural numbers. A finite set $A$ of words of length $n$ over $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ is an independent code for the $q$-cycle when every difference $x = a_1 - a_2$ with $a_1, a_2 \in A$ whose coordinates all lie in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$ is the zero word. For $q \ge 3$ this says exactly that $A$ is an independent set in the $n$-th strong power of the cycle graph $C_q$.

results.title: Cycle codes
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For natural numbers $q$ and $n$, a cycle code of length $n$ modulo $q$ is a finite set of words of length $n$ over $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ that is an independent code for the $q$-cycle.

results.title: Finitely many cycle codes of each length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every nonzero natural number $q$ and every natural number $n$, there are only finitely many cycle codes of length $n$ modulo $q$.

results.title: Rate of a cycle code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $q$, a positive integer $n$ and a cycle code $A$ of length $n$ modulo $q$, the rate of $A$ is $|A|^{1/n}$, the $n$-th root of the number of codewords of $A$, taken in the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$.

results.title: Shannon capacity of the modular cycle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $q$, the Shannon capacity of the $q$-cycle is the supremum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the rates $|A|^{1/n}$ over all positive integers $n$ and all cycle codes $A$ of length $n$ modulo $q$.

results.title: Code rates are at most the cycle capacity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $q$, every positive integer $n$ and every cycle code $A$ of length $n$ modulo $q$, the rate of $A$ is at most the Shannon capacity of the $q$-cycle.

results.title: Codes give lower bounds on the cycle capacity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q$, $n$ and $M$ be natural numbers with $n \ge 1$. If some finite set of words of length $n$ over $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ is an independent code for the $q$-cycle and has exactly $M$ elements, then $M^{1/n}$ is at most the Shannon capacity of the $q$-cycle, as an inequality in $[0, \infty]$.

results.title: BPZ profiles
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A BPZ profile is an arbitrary quadruple of integers, called its code, pairs, auxiliary and neutral coordinates: the four integer coordinates propagated by the valid-tuple product of Buys, Polak and Zuiddam. No validity condition is imposed on the quadruple.

results.title: Product of BPZ profiles
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $i = 1, 2$ let $p_i = (c_i, \pi_i, a_i, z_i)$ be a BPZ profile, with integer code, pairs, auxiliary and neutral coordinates. The product $p_1 \star p_2$ is the BPZ profile with code coordinate $(c_1 - \pi_1)(c_2 - \pi_2) + a_1 \pi_2 + \pi_1 a_2$, pairs coordinate $z_1 \pi_2 + \pi_1 z_2$, auxiliary coordinate $a_1 a_2$ and neutral coordinate $z_1 z_2 + (a_1 - z_1)(a_2 - z_2)$.

results.title: Iterated squaring of BPZ profiles
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Strong power of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph with vertex set $V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. The $k$-th strong power $G^{\boxtimes k}$ is the simple graph whose vertices are the words $x = (x_1, \dots, x_k) \in V^k$ of length $k$, in which two words $x$ and $y$ are adjacent (confusable) when $x \neq y$ and for every $i$ either $x_i = y_i$ or $x_i$ and $y_i$ are adjacent in $G$.

results.title: Shannon capacity of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $\theta$ be a real number. For $k \ge 1$ let $G^{\boxtimes k}$ be the $k$-th strong power of $G$ and $\alpha(G^{\boxtimes k})$ its independence number. The graph $G$ has Shannon capacity $\theta$ when $\alpha(G^{\boxtimes k})^{1/k} \to \theta$ as $k \to \infty$.

results.title: Lovász's theorem: the Shannon capacity of the pentagon
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The cycle graph $C_5$ on five vertices has Shannon capacity $\sqrt{5}$: writing $\alpha(C_5^{\boxtimes k})$ for the independence number of the $k$-th strong power of $C_5$, we have $\alpha(C_5^{\boxtimes k})^{1/k} \to \sqrt{5}$ as $k \to \infty$.
